transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time not thinking about how I look. It sounds kind of vain when I say it, and I know people probably have bigger problems, but… I keep noticing my hairline, and the way my face looks under the lights at the restaurant. I feel like it makes me look old or just… strange.

My coworkers tell me they don’t see what I’m talking about, so maybe I’m making too much of it, but I can’t seem to stop focusing on it.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, trying to hide certain features, or comparing yourself to others, to try to manage how you feel about your appearance?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I do check more than I probably should.

Before a shift, I’ll go into the bathroom and look in the mirror a bunch of times, especially at my hairline. Sometimes I take pictures on my phone from different angles, just to see what other people might be seeing. Then I’ll comb my hair forward and try to get it to sit right.

And I know it’s not helpful, but I’ll sort of replay in my head how guests are going to look at me when I’m out front. Sometimes I get so caught up in it that I’m late getting out there, or I’m already too worked up before I even start. Does that… does that make sense?
Can you tell me more about how you feel your hairline looks? Do you feel like there’s a specific problem with it that others don’t seem to notice?

Yeah… I guess the main thing is I feel like my hairline is too far back, or uneven, and under the restaurant lights it just jumps out at me. Like it makes my whole face look older, kind of harsh or strange.

Other people say they don’t notice it, and I know I probably sound like I’m making too big a deal of it, but to me it feels really obvious. When I’m standing there greeting people, I can’t stop thinking that they’re seeing it too. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Does this concern about your hairline affect your daily life in any way, like making it hard to focus, interact with people, or do your job?

Yeah… it does, more than I’d like to admit.

I try to tell myself I’m still doing my job okay, but I’ve been written up at the restaurant because I’m late getting onto the floor, or I’ve missed shifts when I just couldn’t make myself go in looking like that. I know that probably sounds irresponsible.

And outside of work, I’ve kind of stopped doing things where I might be seen or photographed. Like staff photos… I avoid those. I’ve skipped gallery events and hikes too, even when I wanted to go, because I couldn’t handle people looking at me that way. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Can you tell me if there are times when you feel so distressed about your hairline that it feels impossible to think about anything else?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to let it take over, but honestly, that’s kind of why I’m here.

There are times at work especially where I can’t stop thinking about my hairline, and how my face looks under those restaurant lights. It feels like it makes me look old or strange, and even if coworkers tell me they don’t see what I’m talking about, I can’t really… believe it in the moment.

I’ll be standing there trying to focus on guests, and it’s like my mind keeps snapping back to, “They’re noticing it.” I know that probably sounds excessive, but yes, sometimes it feels hard to think about anything else.
